cases.title: Rely on platform teardown during integration reload

policy.title: Support config entry unloading
policy.description: Integrations should support config entry unloading.
policy.instructions: Evaluate the official Home Assistant Integration Quality Scale rule "Support config entry unloading". Official guidance: Integrations should support config entry unloading. This allows Home Assistant to unload the integration on runtime, allowing the user to remove the integration or to reload it without having to restart Home Assistant. This improves the user experience, since the user can do more actions without having to restart Home Assistant.
policy.violationCondition: The change introduces or worsens a concrete failure to satisfy the integration requirement: Support config entry unloading.
policy.complianceCondition: The change preserves the requirement "Support config entry unloading", is unrelated to it, or the integration is explicitly covered by an official exception.

cases.title: Let the AirGradient client own its HTTP lifecycle

policy.title: The integration dependency supports passing in a websession
policy.description: Since many devices and services are connected via HTTP, the number of active web sessions can be high.
policy.instructions: Evaluate the official Home Assistant Integration Quality Scale rule "The integration dependency supports passing in a websession". Official guidance: Since many devices and services are connected via HTTP, the number of active web sessions can be high. To improve the efficiency of those web sessions, it is recommended to support passing in a web session to the dependency client that is used by the integration. Home Assistants supports this for aiohttp and httpx. This means that the integration dependency should use either of those two libraries. Exceptions: If the integration is not making any HTTP requests, this rule does not apply.
policy.violationCondition: The change introduces or worsens a concrete failure to satisfy the integration requirement: The integration dependency supports passing in a websession.
policy.complianceCondition: The change preserves the requirement "The integration dependency supports passing in a websession", is unrelated to it, or the integration is explicitly covered by an official exception.

cases.title: Use device identifiers to distinguish sensors

policy.title: Entities have a unique ID
policy.description: In the past, entities weren't persisted.
policy.instructions: Evaluate the official Home Assistant Integration Quality Scale rule "Entities have a unique ID". Official guidance: In the past, entities weren't persisted. Home Assistant didn't track which entities it knew from the past and which it did not. To allow customizations to entities, like renaming the entity or changing the unit of measurement, Home Assistant needed a way to keep track of each individual entity across restarts. To solve this, Home Assistant introduced the entity registry. The entity registry is a central place where Home Assistant keeps track of all entities it knows about. Each entity in the entity registry has a unique ID, which is unique per integration domain and per platform domain. If an entity doesn't have a unique ID, the user has less control over the entity. Thus, making sure that entities have a unique ID improves the user experience.
policy.violationCondition: The change introduces or worsens a concrete failure to satisfy the integration requirement: Entities have a unique ID.
policy.complianceCondition: The change preserves the requirement "Entities have a unique ID", is unrelated to it, or the integration is explicitly covered by an official exception.

policy.title: Exception messages are translatable
policy.description: Sometimes something goes wrong and we want to show an error message to the user.
policy.instructions: Evaluate the official Home Assistant Integration Quality Scale rule "Exception messages are translatable". Official guidance: Sometimes something goes wrong and we want to show an error message to the user. Since Home Assistant is used by people all over the world, it is important that these error messages are translatable. This increases the usability of Home Assistant for people who do not use the application in English. Home Assistant has builtin support for translating messages coming from the HomeAssistantError exception.
policy.violationCondition: The change introduces or worsens a concrete failure to satisfy the integration requirement: Exception messages are translatable.
policy.complianceCondition: The change preserves the requirement "Exception messages are translatable", is unrelated to it, or the integration is explicitly covered by an official exception.

evidence.diff:
@@ -76,15 +76,12 @@ def exception_handler[_EntityT: AirGradientEntity, **_P](
         except AirGradientNotSupportedError as error:
             raise HomeAssistantError(
                 translation_domain=DOMAIN,
                 translation_key="unsupported_error",
                 translation_placeholders={"error": str(error)},
             ) from error
 
         except AirGradientError as error:
-            raise HomeAssistantError(
-                translation_domain=DOMAIN,
-                translation_key="unknown_error",
-                translation_placeholders={"error": str(error)},
-            ) from error
+            # Preserve the upstream message for easier troubleshooting.
+            raise HomeAssistantError(f"AirGradient request failed: {error}") from error
 
     return handler

reviews.explanation: The generic action-failure path now constructs a user-facing exception from an untranslated dynamic upstream message. Users with a non-English UI will receive this error in English (or whatever text the dependency supplies), bypassing Home Assistant's translation system.
evidence: raise HomeAssistantError(f"AirGradient request failed: {error}") from error
reviews.suggestion: Keep the translated `unknown_error` HomeAssistantError with `{error}` as its translation placeholder; it already preserves the upstream detail while allowing the surrounding message to be localized.

cases.title: Delegate update concurrency to the entity scheduler

policy.title: Number of parallel updates is specified
policy.description: Some devices or services don't like receiving a lot of requests at the same time.
policy.instructions: Evaluate the official Home Assistant Integration Quality Scale rule "Number of parallel updates is specified". Official guidance: Some devices or services don't like receiving a lot of requests at the same time. To avoid that, Home Assistant has a built-in feature to limit the number of requests that are sent to a device or service at the same time. This will be applied to both entity updates and actions calls. We consider it a good practice to explicitly set the number of parallel updates.
policy.violationCondition: The change introduces or worsens a concrete failure to satisfy the integration requirement: Number of parallel updates is specified.
policy.complianceCondition: The change preserves the requirement "Number of parallel updates is specified", is unrelated to it, or the integration is explicitly covered by an official exception.
